picks.title: The Vulnerability of God with Gila Fine
picks.summary:
Can God be vulnerable? National Jewish Book Award winner Gila Fine explores the stunning talmudic tale of Rabbi Yishmael ben Elisha, who entered the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur and was asked by God for a blessing (Berakhot 7a). What does it mean for an omnipotent God to ask a mortal for help? Through the lens of rabbinic literature, Shakespeare's King Lear, and modern philosophy, Fine reveals the difference between the God of the Bible and the God of the Talmud — and what divine vulnerability teaches us about the relationship between God and humanity. 
Gila Fine is a lecturer in rabbinic lite
picks.reason: Explores divine vulnerability through Talmudic tales and Jewish philosophy.

picks.title: Michelle Farber: Bringing Talmud to the World
picks.summary:
The Talmud is the foundational text of Judaism — every law, every debate, every dissenting opinion preserved across 2,711 pages. For centuries it was accessible only to scholars. That is changing.
Rabbanit Michelle Farber is the founder of Hadran and the host of Daf Yomi for Women, the first and only women's daily Daf Yomi podcast. From her dining room table in Israel, she has built a worldwide movement — bringing daily Talmud study into the lives of thousands of women and men from all backgrounds.
The story of how the Talmud went from the study halls of the few to the daily lives of the many
picks.reason: Profiles a movement making Talmud study accessible to diverse learners worldwide.

picks.title: Michael Weingrad on Contemporary Israeli Poetry
picks.summary: Man is a storytelling animal, and conveying the experience of the human condition in poetry and prose helps us understand and contend with it. That's true in all times and places, and it is why students of a society and its culture have much to learn from its poets. Contemporary Israel is one of the most interesting societies anywhere on earth, and its poets encompass the depth of its culture—God and man, the inescapability of war, human vices large and small. picks.reason: Considers human condition and ethics through contemporary Israeli poetry.
